description: The bar chart illustrates the number of sentences distributed across various text categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories, labeled "Categories," with the individual text labels rotated diagonally for readability. The categories are not sorted in any specific alphabetical or numerical order. The vertical axis represents the numerical values, labeled "Sentences (K)," indicating that the units are in thousands. This axis uses a linear scale with a visible range from 0 to 800, featuring tick marks at regular intervals of 200. The chart consists of eight vertical bars, all colored light red, and each bar is visually emphasized with its exact numerical value annotated directly above it in dark blue text. From left to right, the categories and their corresponding values are Administrative (525), Religion (50), Non-fiction (190), Fiction (35), Law (23), News (902), Science (110), and a final category whose label is completely obscured by a grey rectangular blur, which has a value of 2. The tallest bar represents the News category with 902 thousand sentences, while the shortest bar corresponds to the obscured category with just 2 thousand sentences.
